title: Number Sprint
tagline: Fast sums. Prime splits. Beat your own time.
teaser: Fire off sums against the clock, split numbers into their primes, sweep a board clean of everything that isn't prime, and spell big numbers out in words. Four little Unix number tools, turned into one fast, good-looking game, on a running track or in a glowing atom lab: your pick.

manPage.synopsis: Number Sprint — sums with a forgiving tutor, prime splits, a sieve and numbers in words, against the clock or calm.
manPage.description: Four small BSD number tools in one game: Eamonn McManus's arithmetic drill, whose tutor brings back the numbers you miss until it forgives them; Landon Curt Noll's factor and primes, as splits and a sieve; and number, which spells numerals out in English. Run it on a floodlit track or in an atom lab.

howToPlay: Quick Sums: type each answer; a wrong one stays until you get it, and the numbers you miss come back for practice.
Split numbers into primes, sweep a board clean of everything that is not prime, and turn numbers into words and back.
Rush races the clock and your own best; Calm counts accuracy only. Play the Daily, the campaign or free play.
